newsitem.title: USA: Mead earnings hurt by lower pulp, paper prices.
newsitem.headline: Mead earnings hurt by lower pulp, paper prices.

text.p: Mead Corp., reporting lower results for the quarter and the year, said Thursday its sales and earnings were hurt by substantially lower prices for pulp, paper and containerboard.
The Dayton, Ohio-based paper manufacturer had fourth-quarter profits of $29.2 million, or 55 cents a share. A year earlier it earned $81.6 million, or $1.37 a share.
Sales rose slightly to $1.15 billion from $1.14 billion.

"While 1996 was a difficult year in the market, it was a solid year for Mead," said Steven C. Mason, chairman and chief executive officer. "We significantly strengthened our positions in coated paper and corrugating medium with major growth projects," he said in a statement.
For the year, Mead earned $195.3 million, or $3.57 a share, compared with $350 million, or $6.19 a share in 1995. Sales declined to $4.71 billion from $5.18 billion.
Mead said that demand in some product areas, such as coated paper and corrugated medium paper, was improving. Other areas, such as carbonless and speciality papers, remained strong.
"Overall, however, market and price uncertainties remain," Mason said.
The quarterly results were five cents a share higher than estimates compiled by First Call Inc. Mead's stock was unchanged at $60.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
